summary: Describes how to use PPP over SONET and SDH circuits, the fiber-optic transmission systems used by carriers. It is a standards-track proposal. It was replaced by RFC 2615.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 1619 describes carrying PPP over SONET and SDH circuits. It maps PPP octets into the synchronous payload envelope and specifies the label used to identify PPP; RFC 2615 later obsoleted this memo.

questions: how to use ppp on fiber
how does ppp map into sonet
what does the sonet c2 label indicate
subtitle: Maps PPP frames into SONET and SDH transmission circuits.

tldr.problem: PPP needed a defined way to run over high-speed SONET and SDH point-to-point circuits.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC maps PPP's octet stream into the SONET/SDH Synchronous Payload Envelope, aligns octets with its boundaries, and identifies PPP with a Path Signal Label.

sections.title: PPP on SONET and SDH
sections.content: PPP transports multiprotocol datagrams over point-to-point links. This specification describes using it over SONET and SDH circuits, which are point-to-point by definition. The stated applicability is high-speed private links, such as unused single-mode fiber within a campus.
sections.plainLanguage: PPP can carry network datagrams across a point-to-point link. This memo specifies how to use PPP on SONET and SDH circuits.

sections.title: Mapping PPP into the Payload
sections.content:
PPP treats SONET/SDH as an octet-oriented synchronous link. The octet stream is mapped into the Synchronous Payload Envelope (SPE), with octet boundaries aligned to SPE octet boundaries. The memo says no scrambling is needed during insertion.

The Path Signal Label (C2) uses experimental value 207, hexadecimal cf, to indicate PPP. The H4 Multiframe Indicator is unused and must be zero. The basic rate is STS-3c/STM-1 at 155.520 Mbps, with 149.760 Mbps of available information bandwidth.
sections.plainLanguage: PPP bytes go into the SONET or SDH payload with their byte boundaries aligned. A label marks the payload as PPP, and the H4 indicator stays at zero.

sections.title: Framing and Configuration
sections.content:
PPP framing for octet-synchronous links follows the PPP in HDLC Framing specification. Frames have variable length and may cross SPE boundaries.

The standard LCP synchronous configuration defaults apply. The RFC recommends Magic Number, a 32-bit FCS, and no address/control or protocol field compression. It says PPP does not require physical-layer control signals, though available signals can provide greater functionality and performance.
sections.plainLanguage: PPP uses its standard HDLC framing, and a frame can continue across a payload boundary. The memo recommends a 32-bit frame check sequence and leaving two forms of compression off.

sections.title: Security and Status
sections.content: The memo says security issues are not discussed. RFC 1619 was later obsoleted by RFC 2615, which updated the specification.
sections.plainLanguage: This memo does not discuss security issues. RFC 2615 later replaced it.
